brand.name: Merit
brand.description: Merit turns student projects, CVs, skills, and artifacts into trusted proof profiles recruiters can evaluate beyond the resume.

rails.right: Merit / Proof over pedigree / Talent proven through work
rails.left: Passport / Proof Card / Match Signal / Recruiter Confidence

hero.label: Proof-of-ability platform
hero.lead: Merit should feel like the trusted proof layer for early-career work: elegant enough for students to be proud of, structured enough for recruiters to use, and serious enough for investors to believe.
hero.meta: Proof Card -> Passport -> Match Rationale -> Opportunity

about.label: Brand thesis
about.lead: The V4 identity turns the current warm gallery into premium proof infrastructure. Real student work remains the hero, but recruiter evaluation becomes the organizing system.
about.side_note: Do not make this another portfolio site. Make it hiring signal.

capabilities.label: Brand objects
capabilities.lead: Merit becomes ownable when it consistently names and designs the objects recruiters evaluate.

cards.title: Portable proof identity
cards.body: A public profile that feels more official than a portfolio and more useful than a resume.

cards.title: Work as evidence
cards.body: Each card answers what was built, what it proves, and why it matters for a role.

cards.title: Skills in context
cards.body: Skills are not floating tags. They are backed by project artifacts and outcomes.

cards.title: Explainable fit
cards.body: Recruiters see why a candidate matches, what evidence is strong, and what is missing.

labs.label: Creative directions

cards.title: Premium Future Workforce
cards.body: Institutional trust, precise evidence hierarchy, artifact-first surfaces.

cards.title: Modern Builder Culture
cards.body: More energetic, more maker-led, useful for acquisition but less buyer-authoritative.

cards.title: Elite Talent Discovery
cards.body: Sharp and analytical, strongest for monetization but risks reducing students to scores.

cards.title: Ink / Paper / Signal
cards.body: Gold becomes signal, blue becomes recruiter trust, green becomes validation.

cards.title: Serif / Sans / Mono
cards.body: Serif sells belief, sans runs product, mono marks evidence.

labs.foot: The visual recommendation is Direction A with controlled energy borrowed from B and evidence density borrowed from C.

method.label: Method
method.right: The product should make the transformation visible in every surface.

steps.title: Capture
steps.body: Students add projects, CVs, links, screenshots, decks, repos, and artifacts.

steps.title: Structure
steps.body: Merit asks what was built, what role was played, what skills were demonstrated, and what changed.

steps.title: Surface
steps.body: The passport presents proof cards as recruiter-readable evidence.

steps.title: Match
steps.body: Recruiters see fit rationale, missing evidence, and shortlist confidence.
